resources.string: Buttons, shortcuts and where your games go
andr36oid turns this console into an Android handheld. Games, emulators and apps, all run with the buttons, no touchscreen needed.
Read it, the D-pad then scrolls
You can open this guide again any time from Settings > Quick start guide.
Hold: power menu with Home, the app switcher, Close background apps, Power off and Restart
Menu in apps that have one
The left stick moves around like the D-pad
Hold FN and press a second button. FN on its own still goes to the home screen.
Back to the app you used before
Games go on the EASYROMS partition of the SD card. In a computer, the card shows up as a drive called EASYROMS. On the console, it\'s the EASYROMS storage in the Files app.
Give every system its own folder, named like nes, snes, gb, gba, megadrive or psx. Cards set up for ArkOS or dArkOS already use these names, so their games work as they are.
The console makes these folders on EASYROMS by itself, with a README listing which system goes where.
Daijishou, the home screen, turns those folders into a game library: add a platform and pick its folder on EASYROMS.

RetroArch and PPSSPP come preinstalled. RetroArch already has the cores for NES, SNES, Game Boy, GBA, Mega Drive, Master System, Game Gear, PlayStation, PC Engine, Neo Geo Pocket, WonderSwan, Atari 2600, 7800 and Lynx.
PSP games run in PPSSPP. PlayStation games start without a BIOS, but work best with one in RetroArch\'s system folder.
The emulators are ordinary apps: F-Droid can update them, and you can uninstall them.

Settings > Performance has three profiles. Battery saver for long sessions with older systems, Balanced for everyday use, Performance for PS1, N64 and PSP. The Quick Settings tile switches between them too.
Settings > CPU overclock (experimental) runs the processor faster than standard for demanding games. A restart turns it off. If the console freezes, pick a lower speed.
CPU overclock (experimental), on the same page, runs the processor faster than standard for demanding games. A restart turns it off. If the console freezes, pick a lower speed.
The screen uses the most power. Lower brightness means longer play time.
Hold both sticks pressed in for a second: joystick mouse on or off
Settings > Joystick mouse changes speed, buttons and the combination.
Settings > Button mapping swaps buttons, with profiles for different games.
Locked yourself out? Hold both volume buttons for 5 seconds and every button is back to normal.
The console has no Wi-Fi built in. Plug a USB Wi-Fi adapter into the OTG port, with a USB-C adapter if it needs one, then turn on Wi-Fi in Settings > Network & internet.
